keyVerseText: And Zechariah the son of Meshelemiah was porter of the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.
rootMeaning: The name מְשֶׁלֶמְיָה (Meshelemiah) derives from the Hebrew root שָׁלַם (shâlam), which carries the sense of making amends, repaying, or restoring. Combined with the divine element יָהּ (Yah), the name literally means "whom Jehovah repays" or "ally of Yah." This etymology highlights a deep theological concept of God as one who restores, recompenses, and brings completion or peace, beyond the common English gloss which might simply render it as a proper name without this rich implication.
usageInScripture: The word מְשֶׁלֶמְיָה appears four times in Scripture, consistently as a proper name referring to an individual, specifically an Israelite Levite. The top translations reflect this, with two occurrences translated simply as "of Meshelemiah," one as "was Meshelemiah," and another as "And Meshelemiah," indicating its role as a personal name rather than a common noun. This consistency underscores its identity as a named Levite, a gatekeeper or porter associated with the house of God during David's time.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding מְשֶׁלֶמְיָה as "whom Jehovah repays" enriches our appreciation of God's character as one who faithfully restores and recompenses His people. The Levite Meshelemiah's role as a porter of the sanctuary symbolizes the faithfulness and trustworthiness required to guard God's holy presence, reflecting how God Himself is the ultimate guardian and fulfiller of His covenant promises. This name reminds believers that God is not only a protector but also one who brings restoration and peace, pointing ultimately to Christ who perfectly fulfills God's promise of reconciliation and redemption.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Chronicles 9:21, it is recorded, "And Zechariah the son of Meshelemiah was porter of the door of the tabernacle of the congregation." The mention of Meshelemiah here not only identifies Zechariah’s lineage but also connects him to a legacy of faithful service to God’s sanctuary. The name Meshelemiah, meaning "whom Jehovah repays," enriches this verse by suggesting that this faithful service is undergirded by God’s faithfulness to repay and restore, encouraging believers to trust in God's just and restorative nature as they serve Him.
